title: Insecure Deserialization in HttpRestartServer
analysis:
In `HttpRestartServer.handle(ServerHttpRequest, ServerHttpResponse)`, the server processes HTTP requests destined for the remote restart endpoint. The method directly creates a `java.io.ObjectInputStream` over `request.getBody()` without configuring any deserialization filtering (such as an `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist). When `(ClassLoaderFiles) objectInputStream.readObject()` is executed, arbitrary Java objects sent in the HTTP request body are deserialized. 

If gadget classes (such as those in common third-party libraries or the Spring framework itself) are present on the classpath, an attacker can supply a malicious serialized object payload to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) prior to the class cast to `ClassLoaderFiles`.

Data Path:
- Source: `ServerHttpRequest request.getBody()` (untrusted HTTP request body).
- Sanitization/Validation: None. No `ObjectInputFilter` or type validation is applied to the incoming stream.
- Sink: `objectInputStream.readObject()` at line 74.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Generate a gadget chain payload using a tool like ysoserial (e.g. CommonsCollections or Spring gadget payload) and send it as the HTTP POST body to the remote restart endpoint:
```http
POST /.~~spring-boot!~/restart HTTP/1.1
Host: target-app:8080
X-AUTH-TOKEN: <devtools-secret>
Content-Length: 1337
Content-Type: application/octet-stream

<raw bytes of serialized Java gadget payload executing e.g. calc.exe or touch /tmp/pwned>
```
